## C-01: Lease as Warpgate role assignment

- Provider: bastion; consumer: agent
- Interface: /users/:id/roles and /users/:id/roles/:role_id with expires_at (warpgate-admin/src/api/users.rs)
- Permission: AccessRolesAssign, on the edge host's loopback only
- Status: built

A signed lease in the bundle becomes a role assignment with expires_at = lease end; an early end or a revocation in a newer bundle revokes it. Assignments the agent did not make are drift, reported to KeyClerk; KeyClerk (through the agent) is the only writer (KeyClerk 0013 D2). Built and unit-tested (agent internal/apply apply_test.go and regress_test.go: grants with expires_at, a moved expiry, drift reported not guessed; internal/agent agent_test.go: revocation and offline lease end on the fakes).

## C-02: Session approval from a signed lease

- Provider: bastion; consumer: agent
- Interface: GET /session-approvals, POST /session-approvals/:id/approve\|reject, approvals stream (session_approvals.rs)
- Permission: ApproveSessions, on the edge host's loopback only
- Status: needed

The agent approves a pending session only if a valid signed lease in its current bundle covers that person, target and moment, including any second key the policy required when KeyClerk granted it; otherwise it rejects with the reason. No live round trip to the core is needed, so approval works while the edge is cut off.

## C-03: LDAP lease credential

- Provider: facade; consumer: agent
- Interface: the facade's admin API on loopback (lldap: GraphQL and its password-set flow on http_host=127.0.0.1), never the LDAP port the legacy system binds to; RFC 3062 password modify only if the facade separates admin binds (R-02)
- Permission: a facade admin bound to the edge host's loopback
- Status: needed
- KeyClerk: KeyClerk 0014 (v0.17.0), docs/keyclerk-edge-interface.md

Lease start: the agent sets the person's facade password to a fresh random value and sends it encrypted to that person's own key, derived from their passkey (WebAuthn PRF / hmac-secret) and registered in KeyClerk; the desk relays ciphertext only. Where the system binds once per login, the agent rotates again after the first successful bind, and alerts on a bind with no matching session of the holder. Lease end: rotate, send nothing. No fallback to a desk key (decision 0009).

## C-04: Signed lease bundles

- Provider: clerk; consumer: agent
- Interface: KeyClerk 0013 D3: signed, serial-numbered bundles with a ceiling, a serial floor and horizons per class
- Permission: the edge's own enrolment credential, one per edge
- Status: built
- KeyClerk: KeyClerk 0014 (v0.17.0), docs/keyclerk-edge-interface.md

The agent pulls bundles outbound, refuses a bundle with a lower serial, a wrong signer or past its horizon, and reports what it applied. Past a class horizon it ends that class's leases; visit leases end at their own signed window (decision 0007; fail closed, decision 0005 point 3). Bundle entries outside the edge's ceiling (C-10) are refused. Built and unit-tested (agent internal/kcedge kcedge_test.go: the verifier against KeyClerk's conformance set testdata/edge.json, serial floors, signers and class horizons included, plus fuzzing; internal/state state_test.go: floors only rise; internal/agent agent_test.go: a lease applied and reported, a replayed bundle refused, a lease ended at its own time while the desk is down).

## C-06: Pre-staged visit lease

- Provider: bastion; consumer: agent
- Interface: Warpgate user credentials (SSH public key) plus C-01 role assignment with expires_at
- Permission: credential and role assignment on the edge's loopback only
- Status: built
- KeyClerk: KeyClerk 0014 (v0.17.0), docs/keyclerk-edge-interface.md

A visit lease in the bundle installs the operator's hardware-held ssh-ed25519 public key (sk-ssh once U-01 lands) and a role assignment for the window; both are removed at the window's end even if the edge is cut off. Works with no network at all (decision 0006). The agent installs only sk-ssh-ed25519 and ssh-ed25519 keys, assigns the role only when it reaches no target the visit does not name, and runs the ceiling's visit rules (an assured edge), which KeyClerk's reference verifier leaves out. Built and unit-tested (agent internal/apply visit_test.go); not yet live, since this agent attests basic.

## C-07: Carried visit lease

- Provider: agent; consumer: person
- Interface: the agent's local access port (R-11)
- Permission: KeyClerk's lease signature plus proof of possession of the bound hardware key
- Status: needed
- KeyClerk: KeyClerk 0014 (v0.17.0), docs/keyclerk-edge-interface.md

The agent accepts a lease signed to the operator for this edge, inside its window and above the serial floor, then installs it as in C-06. Refuses a lease for another edge, a replayed lease, or one older than the floor.

## C-08: Phoned unlock

- Provider: agent; consumer: person, clerk
- Interface: challenge shown at the edge; short response code issued by KeyClerk (R-13)
- Permission: a per-edge unlock key shared by the edge and the core only
- Status: needed
- KeyClerk: KeyClerk 0014c (v0.19.0), docs/keyclerk-edge-interface.md

Single use, bound to edge, person, target, nonce and duration; the approver is a second person; rate-limited and recorded. A wrong code counts toward lock-out.

## C-09: Break-glass credential

- Provider: agent; consumer: person, clerk
- Interface: one sealed local credential per legacy system, escrowed in the organisation's password manager (R-06)
- Permission: dual control of the escrow; the agent rotates it after any use
- Status: needed
- KeyClerk: KeyClerk 0014 (v0.17.0), docs/keyclerk-edge-interface.md

Use is detected (facade or Warpgate sign-in with the break-glass account), recorded in the hash-chained edge log, rotated as soon as the agent can, and reported to KeyClerk as an incident for review on reconnect.

## C-10: Per-edge ceiling

- Provider: agent; consumer: clerk
- Interface: ceiling as data sealed by the officer (kc-edge-ceiling-v2, carried in the bundle exactly as sealed) read by KeyClerk's ceiling.rego (KeyClerk 0014, 0014d; 0007 amended)
- Permission: only the edge officer's signature changes it; the officer is not a core administrator
- Status: built
- KeyClerk: KeyClerk 0014 (v0.17.0), docs/keyclerk-edge-interface.md

The agent admits only what both the core's signed policy and the ceiling allow (persons or roles, targets, maximum lease, maximum offline validity, lease classes, hardware profile, remote-reach mode and ports). A ceiling with a lower serial or a wrong signer is refused. Hardware facts come from attestation, not from the ceiling (0007). Built as a Go port of ceiling.rego (agent internal/kcedge ceiling.go) until the signed policy module runs in process; unit-tested against KeyClerk's ceiling vectors (kcedge_test.go TestCeilingPolicyMatchesKeyClerk and the ceilings family in TestConformanceFamilies) and on the fakes (agent_test.go TestALeaseOutsideTheCeilingIsNotApplied). Not yet: hardware attestation (the agent attests basic, so visit leases are refused), and remote-reach mode and ports are checked for form but not yet applied.

## C-05: Broker sign-in and approval proofs

- Provider: broker; consumer: clerk, bastion
- Interface: OIDC; KeyClerk 0003 (SCIM) and 0006 (approvals as signatures)
- Permission: per KeyClerk 0003
- Status: built

Passkey-only sign-in by default; approvals are the approver's own fresh sign-in. Warpgate side (decision 0010): one confidential PKCE client per edge with no roles claim (KeyClerk watches its mappers), auto_create_users off, e-mail admin-editable only. KeyClerk's approval proofs (KeyClerk 0006) are off by default there; ReliKey's shipped configuration sets `approvals.proofs: required` (a supported, CI-covered KeyClerk setting, confirmed 2026-10-23).

## C-11: Signed updates

- Provider: mirror; consumer: host
- Interface: a signed update manifest naming image digests; images pulled from the core's mirror (F-18)
- Permission: an update-signing key separate from the lease-signing key; the edge pins its public key
- Status: needed

The edge applies only images whose digest the current manifest names and whose provenance (build attestation, SBOM) was verified at pin time; a manifest with a lower serial is refused; rollout is staged by edge group.

## C-12: Recording backfill

- Provider: org-store; consumer: agent
- Interface: the organisation's S3-compatible store; Warpgate's own upload does not retry (U-10)
- Permission: write-only to the edge's own prefix
- Status: needed
- KeyClerk: KeyClerk 0014 (v0.17.0), docs/keyclerk-edge-interface.md

Recordings left in the local store are uploaded when the uplink returns, their hashes chained in the edge log and acknowledged by the core before deletion. Below the store's free-disk floor no new recorded session starts.
